title: Witness · The commissioning rite
summary:
**Original lore · provisional**

For its commissioning rite, a pilot walks once around an unpowered chassis. Somewhere behind the armor, a shutter follows them. From then on, the frame always knows where that person is.

I’d give it a **headless wedge-shaped core** with a recessed band of inspection windows around its upper edge. A pale ceramic shutter travels behind the band. Wherever it stops, the window above it reads as a brow and the dark gap below as an eye.

Its best use might be a rival encounter: you quick-boost past it, its legs skid several metres, and its attention travels around the stationary hull to meet you on the far side.

items.title: Witness in the casting yard
items.alt: A headless wedge-shaped combat mech braces on long graphite-sleeved legs. Its prow and rifle point right, while a pale shutter faces the viewer from a dark window band along its flank.
items.body:
The pale ceramic shutter rides behind a band of dark inspection windows. It has tracked the viewer around the flank while the hull and induction rifle still point across the yard. One foot scrapes the wet concrete as the machine brakes.

The induction rifle and shorter pulse driver occupy the hands. Two outboard pylons carry the vertical-launch cassette and folding beam unit above the window band. The twin booster bells and lateral hip port sit below the cockpit.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/witness/casting-yard-v001.png)
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make one full-body hero concept image of WITNESS, an original eight-metre PILOTED combat mech. Its commissioning rite bound it to the person who first walked around its unpowered chassis. It has a terrible gift for recognizing you. Show the instant you dodge past the rival: its body and weapons are still committed to the old bearing, but its gaze has already found YOU around the side of its hull. Express all of this in a single physically legible portrait with no words.

Primary distinctive shape: a fast, completely HEADLESS biped. The entire forward-raked cockpit is one sealed compact wedge, a clipped chisel-shaped prow with long sloping surfaces and a clean, low, uninterrupted roofline. The prow and the guns point diagonally toward SCREEN RIGHT. The viewer sees the broad near flank AND the angled front return of this wedge. At the top third of the core, a continuous recessed horizontal belt of SMOKED inspection windows wraps around the near flank, front corner and front surface. Slender bronze mullions and a fine internal runner show that ONE pale ivory ceramic shutter can physically travel around this belt. Put this lone ivory slider halfway along the near FLANK, well behind the nose, broadside looking straight at the viewer; a dark little off-center aperture in the ceramic under the overhanging armor brow accidentally makes an eye. All the other panes, especially those at the nose, are empty and black. At thumbnail size, a single conspicuous pale oblong in the dark wraparound band, staring sideways while the rest of the machine looks past us. No separate sensor head, face, turret, floating eye, biological eyeball, duplicate lenses or neon visor. The glass should look recessed in a continuous band, not like a row of headlights. Under the belt: a sealed pilot hatch in overlapping petrol-grey steel and a few small access rungs. No religious costume or decoration: the occult element is entirely the displaced gaze.

Light-to-medium frame with quick narrow hips, generous negative space around articulated shoulders, slim functional arms, forward-set core. Long, load-bearing, unnervingly natural bowed Gekko-like legs: charcoal stretch sleeves continuous from the armored upper thighs to the visible mechanical knees, fabric folds around a heavily loaded knee, exposed steel ankle yokes, broad split mechanical toes. Legs visibly capable of walking. Freeze a restrained lateral braking slide: near foot planted and dragging a short chalky scrape in concrete, far heel gathering under its hips, upper wedge still level, faint residual jet from the exposed side port. No running stride, crouched superhero, big explosion or limb motion blur. Keep hip line, arm lengths and cockpit human occupancy plausible.
Armored Core-inspired equipment design and balance. TWO visibly independently gripped mech-scale weapons: near hand around a clear UNDERBODY grip on a long low-slung industrial induction rifle, barrel aimed along the prow toward screen right, neutral wrist and heavy forearm aligned; the other hand carries a shorter faceted pulse driver with a squared emitter low on the far side, visible separately. Massive enough to need a mech, controlled enough to leave silhouette lean. TWO slim outboard BACK weapon pylons rising from the lower rear core and arcing OUT so the wraparound viewing belt remains open: one neat vertical-launch cassette and one folding long-barrel beam unit. Distinct weapons with exposed mount hinges, both stowed clear of the torso's unbroken low top. Two compact heat-stained directional exhaust bells LOW aft and a flush quick-boost port on the outer hip, discernible below the mounts. Exactly two arms, two legs, four weapons.
Camera: a SINGLE portrait, near-square or 4:5, lightly low vantage in front quarter of the near side, the chassis's straight heading and line of attention strongly distinct. Complete boots and all four weapons inside generous frame edges, readable open spaces around all forms. Premium cinematic industrial concept art with convincing patinated field hardware: desaturated blue-grey painted steel, old blackened aluminum, rubbed edges and faded oxide-red panel identifiers, the ivory shutter by far the palest accent on the mech. Late overcast oblique daylight catching the shutter, giving glass and curved sleeves distinct surfaces. Quiet abandoned casting yard with a distant tiny maintenance door, blank cool concrete and standing ground shadows, atmospheric depth. Crisp fine material work on resolved large forms, deliberate grim military design, a disturbing mundane object. No lettering, inset, UI, occult sigils, horns or captions.

items.title: References used
items.body:
The smooth mask and its small apertures were the face reference cited in Witness’s original pitch. The design translated that impression into a pale shutter and a dark gap beneath an armored brow. The traveling shutter and its recognition rite came from the pitch. [Nivanh Chanthara’s mask study](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/788411478568823397/)

Armored Core informed the two hand weapons, two outboard back pylons and separate low rear and side boosters. The painting also drew on the shared Gekko-like leg direction for the bowed, sleeved leg taking the braking load. [Armored Core VI assembly manual](https://www.fromsoftware.jp/manual/armoredcore6/ps5/customize.html) · [Official visual gallery](https://www.armoredcore.net/gallery.html)
